segments.translation: the doves came back in and said kindly: "Aschenputtel, shall we pick out the vetches for you?"
segments.note: The sentence begins mid-sentence at the top of the page. The source has the typo "dte" for "die".

segments.translation: "Yes, — the bad ones into the little crop, the good ones into the little pot."
Pick, pick! pick, pick! it went as fast as if twelve hands were there.
And when they were finished, the doves said: "Aschenputtel, do you also want to go to the ball and dance?"
segments.note: The source ends the question with a full stop inside the quotation mark; it is translated as a question.

segments.translation: "Oh my God, it said, how can I go there in my dirty clothes?"
"Go to the little tree on your mother's grave, shake it and wish yourself beautiful clothes, but come back before midnight."
— then Aschenputtel went out, shook the little tree and said:
"Little tree, shake and shiver yourself, throw down beautiful clothes for me!"
Hardly had it said this when there lay before it a splendid silver dress, pearls, silk stockings with silver clocks, and silver slippers, and whatever else belonged with them.
segments.note: "Zwickeln" refers to the ornamental clocks (gussets) on stockings.

segments.translation: Aschenputtel carried everything home, and when it had washed and dressed, it was as beautiful as a rose that the dew has washed.
